subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: Should non-owner, unknown, and ambient turns retain stable model-visible schemas for `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` while immutable current-turn policy denies execution before hooks and side effects?
rationale: Tests establish that execution remains blocked, but they cannot decide the intended security presentation contract for capabilities unavailable to the current turn.

options.title: Accept runtime-enforced visibility
options.body: Keep stable schemas for cache reuse with immutable pre-hook denial, capability checks, and revocation enforcement.

options.title: Keep schemas hidden
options.body: Reject the presentation change and redesign cache stability without exposing unavailable protected schemas.

options.title: Split the security scope
options.body: Land provider and delivery cache fixes separately while deferring protected-schema visibility.

recommendation.title: Accept runtime-enforced visibility
recommendation.body: Keep stable schemas for cache reuse with immutable pre-hook denial, capability checks, and revocation enforcement.

likelyOwner.reason: The sampled history indicates broad ownership across the affected agent and queue architecture, making this the best available routing candidate for the cross-cutting security contract.
